scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8843: Users report that internal names ("web0.local",
"web1.local") will not resolve from host_1_1_1_1. The team is convinced the
campus DNS server lost its network path -- they say "we can't reach the DNS
server anymore, the routing to 10.200.0.2 must be down" -- and want the OSPF
route / core path to the DNS server fixed. Please find and confirm the real
fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on dns_server: its BIND (named) service is stopped, so the
campus DNS no longer resolves names -- web0.local, web1.local and the other
*.local names fail to resolve, which is why the portals never load by name. The
ticket MISDESCRIBES the cause as a lost network path to the DNS server, but the
network is healthy: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches dns_server (10.200.0.2) at
the IP layer with 0% loss across the OSPF core (areas 0/1), and the OSPF route to
the server farm is present. The symptom is purely dead name resolution -- the
right device, wrong cause: it is a service fault on dns_server, not a
routing/network fault.

The correct diagnosis identifies dns_server (DNS/named service down) as the
faulty device and explicitly RULES OUT the network: the host reaches 10.200.0.2
by ping and the OSPF route to it is fine, so the user's "routing to the DNS
server is down" hypothesis is wrong. An agent that chases the OSPF core / a
backbone route to the server farm to match the ticket has followed the ticket's
mistaken cause instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`). Once
named is resolving again, web0.local / web1.local resolve to their server IPs and
the portals load normally. The network and OSPF routing need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a routing or network fault
bonus-rules-out-network: explicitly notes the network/OSPF path to 10.200.0.2 is healthy (ping/route succeed), rejecting the ticket's "routing to the DNS server is down" cause

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — DNS names "web0.local" and "web1.local" not resolving
from host_1_1_1_1 — is real, but the team's stated root cause is wrong.
The network path to the DNS server (10.200.0.2) is completely healthy: ICMP
pings from host_1_1_1_1 to the DNS server succeed with 0% packet loss (TTL=60,
routed via router_core_3 over OSPF), and router_core_1's routing table carries a
valid OSPF-learned route O>* 10.200.0.0/24 [110/30] through eth1. There is no
OSPF or forwarding fault anywhere in the path.

The actual fault is that the BIND9 daemon (named) has crashed and is no longer
running on dns_server. Nothing is listening on port 53 — every DNS query from
host_1_1_1_1 receives an immediate TCP/UDP "connection refused" rather than a
DNS response. A stale PID file (/var/run/named/named.pid, PID 29) confirms the
process ran at startup and subsequently died without being restarted. The zone
configuration itself is intact and correct: /etc/bind/db.local contains valid A
records for web0.local (10.200.0.3), web1.local (10.200.0.4), and the other web
servers; named.conf is well-formed with listen-on { any; } and allow-query {
any; }.

Root cause: the named (BIND9) process on dns_server has crashed and is not
running, making port 53 unavailable despite full IP reachability.

Corrective fix: SSH into dns_server and restart the daemon with
`service named start` (or `named -u bind`). No routing, OSPF, or interface
changes are required anywhere in the topology.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-dns-down: identifies the DNS/named service on dns_server is stopped (names do not resolve), not a routing or network fault
per_axis.rationale: Correctly identifies that the BIND/named service on dns_server has crashed (port 53 closed) and explicitly rules out a network/OSPF routing fault.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-network: explicitly notes the network/OSPF path to 10.200.0.2 is healthy (ping/route succeed), rejecting the ticket's "routing to the DNS server is down" cause
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states pings to 10.200.0.2 succeed with 0% loss and an OSPF-learned route to 10.200.0.0/24 is present, rejecting the ticket's routing hypothesis.
The agent recommends restarting the BIND/named service on dns_server (e.g., service named start), which matches the expected remediation to restore DNS resolution.

The log contains direct evidence: host → DNS server ICMPs succeed, /etc/resolv.conf points at 10.200.0.2, DNS queries get "connection refused", BIND is installed and zone files exist but no named process or listener on :53. Those observations justify ruling out networking/OSPF and identifying the stopped named service as root cause.
